statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and scheme $W$ with the strict quotient notation of [def-trf-isomorphism-strict-quotient-models]. Let $S$ be any simultaneous derived coefficient-system calculus [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and $r$ any K-injective-normalized Roos realization model [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. There exists a natural isomorphism $\rho$, on all flat-term K-flat complexes, from localization $q$ followed by $S.{\rm reduction}$ and total limit to $D_W$ followed by $H$ and derived localization $Q$, satisfying $\operatorname{TrfCompletionRoosNormalized}(S,r,\rho)$. Thus its formula holds for every whole-system adjunction-coherent simultaneous presentation $K,e,\kappa$, including the actual strict tower isomorphism on sections and the specified derived comparison $e$, without boundedness or completeness assumptions.

proof.text: Choose the ordinary and derived quotient models for the supplied calculus using fixedCalculusModels. On good complexes the reductionComparison components are isomorphisms and assemble naturally. Compose this natural isomorphism with the restriction localization comparison, the given Roos comparison, and the ordinary strict quotient tower isomorphism. For any coherent presentation, coherentQuotientModelComparison factors its specified e as the canonical comparison followed by the localization of a strict system isomorphism a. Restrict a inverse and compose with the ordinary tower comparison to obtain the required section-normalized tower isomorphism. Naturality of the Roos bridge along a and functorial cancellation of a followed by a inverse prove the full displayed limit equation. No derived evaluation is used to detect equality of maps.

old_proof.text: Choose the flat-term K-flat resolution $q:Q\to N$. The derived-system evaluation calculus represents $\mathcal R_YN$ by the single strict system $(Q_n)_n$, not by unrelated choices of its evaluations. Thus $D=U_Y(Q_n)_n$ represents its restricted strict tower. The definition of the ambient completed pullback represents $P_gN$ by $H(C)$, and the normalized strict Roos comparison represents $\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YN$ by $H(D)$. Its hypotheses hold on both sites: they are small in the fixed module universe and countable products of modules over either completed ring sheaf are exact. Neither identification requires $N$ to be derived complete or bounded.

old_proof.text: The functors just used invert every quasi-isomorphism in $\mathcal P$. For $H(C(-))$ this is clause (1) of the well-definedness theorem for the ambient operations. For $GH(D(-))$, the derived-system calculus identifies $D(-)$ on this class with the restriction of the functor $U_Y\mathcal R_Y$, the normalized strict Roos construction is a functor on the derived tower category, and exact $G$ sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus the canonical comparisons identify these two functors with the restrictions of $P_g$ and $G\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_Y$ respectively. These are comparisons of functors on strict systems and their localizations, not a claim that individual projections determine maps between derived limits.

use the simultaneous reduction presentation of a flat-term K-flat
complex, rather than choosing its finite evaluations separately. Restrict its whole
system to completed modules. Each finite presentation kappa induces a restricted
isomorphism. The presentation's transition compatibility makes these maps an
isomorphism of strict towers a; the restriction and evaluation section identifications
give the stated section formula. Apply the normalized Roos bridge to this entire
system and then H(a). Naturality of the simultaneous reduction presentation and of
the bridge makes the result a natural isomorphism rho on good complexes. For another
presentation, compare the two entire derived systems through their specified maps e.
The same transition-compatible evaluation maps identify the strict towers. Functoriality
of the bridge then gives the displayed equation for that presentation too. Equivalently,
on simultaneous K-injectives this is the ordinary compatible limit tuple with zero
shifted coordinate; the normalization of r and naturality extend that computation to
all systems. No choice of unrelated evaluation maps, derived completeness, or
boundedness is used.
